model_rule: Territorial possession is not equivalent to usable operational/economic control. Track physical possession, transport utility, airfield utility, administration/security, and economic extraction separately.

Changsha.river_crossing_and_port: PARTIAL_BY_21_22_MAY; ferries/pontoons and limited wharf use restored, major fixed crossings still damaged
Changsha.rail_road: NORTHBOUND_FEED_PARTIAL_BY_22_23_MAY; local Changsha-Xiangtan movement usable with interruptions; full through-capacity not credited
Changsha.airfield: fighter/recon servicing PARTIAL by 22-23 May; medium/heavy sustained operations not yet credited
Changsha.administration_security: Japanese military control first; Nanjing police/railway/municipal cadres enter progressively 20-24 May under Japanese key-node supervision
Changsha.economic_extraction: LOW_INITIAL. Registries, markets and tax offices begin reopening, but evacuation, sabotage and stock removal prevent immediate fiscal windfall

Xiangtan.transport_role: PARTIAL rail/river transshipment node; repair crews prioritize this because it is essential for continued southward supply
Xiangtan.administration_security: MIXED Japanese engineering/security core plus Nanjing rear-security elements
Xiangtan.airfield: DENIED_TO_CHINA; limited Japanese tactical use only after repair checks

Chinese_rewired_network.command: IX War Area command/service core displaced south rather than destroyed
Chinese_rewired_network.transport: Hengyang-Leiyang-Chenzhou system assumes a larger share of rail/road storage and redistribution
Chinese_rewired_network.air: Fourteenth Air Force/CACW use Hengyang-Lingling/Kweilin depth and temporary fields; Changsha/Xiangtan no longer treated as available bases
Chinese_rewired_network.fiscal_security: Chongqing loses direct access to Changsha/Xiangtan urban-tax/transport nodes but retains clandestine/local resistance networks; no claim of complete Japanese political control

node_transfer_interpretation: By 24 May Japan has enough operational transfer to use Changsha-Xiangtan as a forward campaign platform, but not enough to count the region as fully pacified or economically self-supporting. Continued advance creates a real rear-security burden which Nanjing can partially absorb, not erase.
